children: Trustmark reported third-quarter 2026 net income of $58.1 million, or $1.00 per diluted share. Revenue was $207.1 million, while net interest income on a fully taxable equivalent basis increased 1.2% from the prior quarter to $170.6 million. The company’s operating diluted EPS, a non-GAAP measure, was also $1.00.
Revenue totaled $207.1 million in the third quarter.
Net interest income (FTE) was $170.6 million, up 1.2% quarter over quarter; net interest margin was 3.84%, unchanged from the prior quarter.
Pre-provision net revenue, a non-GAAP measure, was $72.7 million.
Net income was $58.1 million, compared with $63.5 million in the prior quarter and $56.8 million a year earlier.
Diluted EPS was $1.00; operating diluted EPS, a non-GAAP measure, was also $1.00.
Trustmark completed a sale-leaseback of 34 branch properties and entered into 15-year triple-net leases, with renewal options. It continued operating the locations as branches.
After reclassifying its held-to-maturity securities as available for sale, the company sold lower-yielding securities and bought higher-yielding securities as part of a portfolio restructuring.
Loan balances grew 2.4% year over year, supported by commercial and industrial, residential mortgage, construction, consumer, and other loans and leases, despite elevated commercial loan payoffs.
Credit quality remained strong: nonperforming assets were 0.40% of loans held for investment and held for sale, and net charge-offs were 0.03% of average loans.
Wealth management revenue increased 2.2% quarter over quarter and 13.9% year over year.
